title: Post collection imputation - Foreign Tourist In Poland
text: Pilot study for imputation - accommodation establishments

title: Post collection imputation - Foreign Tourist In Poland
text:
Type of accomodation establisments
Tourist accommodation establishments regardless of the type, owner, and location, as well as establishments with other purposes (not related to tourism) that are temporarily used by tourists (e.g., student dormitories, sports and recreation centers).
Tourist accommodation establishments classified into the following activity groups according to NACE Rev. 2 classification:

55.1 – hotels and similar accommodation,
55.2 – holiday and other short-stay accommodation,
55.3 – camping grounds, recreational vehicle parks and trailer parks. The study covers 20 types of tourist accommodation establishments.

title: Post collection imputation - Foreign Tourist In Poland
text:
About survey
KT-1: Report on the occupancy of tourist accommodation establishments:

Mandatory monthly survey of accommodation establishments with 10 or more bed-places.
Census survey of 14,859 establishments.
The deadline for submitting reports is the 10th day after the reporting month. In practice, establishments report throughout the entire month.
Unit response rate is approximately 80% and varies due to seasonality.
Item non-response pertains mostly to foreign tourist data.

title: Post collection imputation - Foreign Tourist In Poland
text:
About Data
Range of collected data

Establishment name, type, address and category of establishment
Months of operation
Rooms and bed places
Occupancy (tourists and nights spent) during the surveyed month
Occupancy (tourists and nights spent) by foreign tourists with respect to country of residence
Categorical and count data

The goal of Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is to understand the main characteristics of a dataset, identify patterns and relationships, detect anomalies and missing values, and generate insights that can guide further analysis or modeling. # Reading a data The synthetic data were generated using the synthetizer package available in R. Therefore, the pyreadr library is used to import the data into Python. The tourism dataset is stored in an .rds file and can be loaded using the following code:
Code
import pyreadr
df = pyreadr.read_r('synthetic data/WP9_S2_Tourism_synt.rds').popitem()[1]

title: Explanatory Data Analysis
text:
Structure of tourism data:

Dataset description
The dataset contains information about tourism establishments and tourist activity in Poland. Each row represents an establishment, identified by its REGON number. The dataset includes information about the type and location of the establishment, as well as data on domestic and foreign tourists.
The main variables include:

REGON – unique identifier of the establishment.
RO – type of tourism establishment.
WON – voivodeship (województwo ) where the establishment is located.
KKR – country of origin of tourists.
D8R1 – number of foreign tourists.

Due to the large size of the dataset, further analyses will be limited to the five countries with the highest number of foreign tourists. This will allow us to reduce the size of the dataset while focusing on the most significant tourist markets.
